Cc: Novamed DevOps <devops@novamed.com>, security@novamed.com
Date: 2027-03-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Novamed: subprocessor roster + SIG/CAIQ evidence request

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our procurement security review we need a consolidated subprocessor roster and your completed SIG questionnaire or CAIQ where available. Our security team is particularly interested in key management residency (where keys are stored/managed) and any processors that touch telemetry/usage data.

Can you provide the following by EOD Tuesday (2027-03-11)?
- CSV roster with provider name, purpose, data types processed, and residency (country)
- SIG or CAIQ answers if available (we can accept a spreadsheet)
- SOC 2 artifact summary (dates, scope)

If helpful we can schedule a short call to walk through edge cases.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Tran
Head of Security Ops, Novamed

Laura —

Appreciate the clarity. We're on it. Quick plan:
1) I'll attach an export of our canonical subprocessor roster (CSV) with the fields you requested.
2) Marissa will attach the SIG/CAIQ draft answers and a SOC 2 summary PDF.
3) Jonas will add a short KMS residency matrix with residency and whether keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed.

If anything in the roster looks sensitive we can redact contact emails, but the residency and scope fields will be complete. If EOD Tuesday is firm we can do a short sync tomorrow 08:30 PT to run through exceptions — otherwise we'll deliver the package to your shared Drive link and ping HubSpot.

Deliverables (expected): redwood_subprocessor_roster_20270309.csv, redwood_sig_answers_v1.xlsx, soc2-summary-2026.pdf, kms_residency_matrix_20270311.xlsx

Dylan

Thanks Marissa, Dylan — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our security reviewers:

1) SIG QnA: We have a handful of deeper questions around control IDs related to key rotation and HSM usage (especially for billing and exports). Can your team call out which controls map to HSM-backed keys vs software KMS?
2) Residency: For the three onshore-only processors you flagged, can you confirm contractual residency language (we need an excerpt stating data will remain in US jurisdiction)?
3) Evidence delivery: please upload the docs to the Drive folder (shared link) and comment in HubSpot deal HS-23456 when completed.

If you can answer (1) and (2) in-line here we'll triage; otherwise we'll schedule the short call.

Laura
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Tran <laura.tran@novamed.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-11T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novamed: subprocessor roster + SIG/CAIQ evidence request

Laura — quick answers inline for the key management questions: 

- HSM-backed keys: Production signing keys for the inference runtime and export encryption keys are stored in our HSM-backed KMS (partner: KeyForge) located in us-east-1. Control mapping: SIG control KMS-02 and KMS-04 reference HSM key generation and FIPS-140-2 Level 3 attestations — supporting evidence attached.
- Software KMS: Ephemeral session tokens and developer sandbox keys use our software KMS backed by envelope encryption; mapped to SIG control KMS-07.
- Contracts excerpt: for the three onshore processors we've attached contract excerpts that include residency clauses and data-at-rest residency commitments. See attachment kms_residency_matrix_20270311.xlsx and subproc_contract_excerpts.zip (attachment).

I'll also drop a short summary into the HubSpot deal and upload the files to the Drive folder. We can expand any control mapping you want on the call.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal, Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference
(attachment: kms_residency_matrix_20270311.xlsx)
